excerpts./plan/formulation: Grover-style amplitude amplification over n-bit assignments x in {0,1}^n. The oracle marks x iff conforms(x, clauses, locked) is true, i.e. all locked equalities hold and every rule clause has at least one literal equal to x. Empty clauses are true. Repeated and contradictory literals are handled by the Boolean predicate exactly as classical conforms does. The classical contract additionally requires returning the first conforming assignment in feature order (False before True), or retaining current if it already conforms; this ordering is not directly provided by Grover and must be addressed separately.
excerpts./plan/input_encoding: n qubits represent the Boolean feature vector. Clause and locked data are classical compile-time parameters embedded in the reversible oracle circuit; if parameterized loading is used, its qubit and gate costs must be included. Ancilla workspace is needed for literal equality tests, 3-way OR per clause, AND across clauses, and locked equality conjunction. No free data loading or coherent memory is assumed.
excerpts./plan/output_decoding: Measure the n decision qubits in the computational basis, decode the bitstring to a feature assignment, and classically verify conforms against the original clauses and locked map. A measured candidate must be verified before returning. The exact first-in-feature-order requirement is unresolved: simple Grover samples among marked states and does not guarantee the lexicographically first satisfying assignment. No-solution handling is also unresolved: if no assignment conforms, Grover may yield no marked outcome, and a separate quantum-counting or classical exhaustive no-solution policy is required to return unavailable with null proposal exactly as classical complete does.
/plan/assumptions: Finite Boolean search space of size 2^n is explicitly representable.
The predicate conforms can be compiled into a reversible oracle with accounted ancillas.
Classical inputs and outputs; no workload, quantum hardware, encoding-cost or advantage evidence supplied.
Classical verification of any measured candidate is available.
Shots and error mitigation are sufficient to detect a marked state with a specified confidence, but no such threshold is supplied.
/plan/risks: Exact ordering semantics (first conforming in feature order, False before True) are not preserved by straightforward Grover search.
No-solution case is not reliably distinguished by Grover alone without quantum counting or a classical exhaustive check.
Oracle construction and ancilla workspace may dominate resources for small n, where classical enumeration is already trivial.
Probabilistic measurement outcomes require repeated shots and classical post-selection; exactness is not guaranteed.
No workload, size cap, hardware or advantage evidence is provided; practical speedup is unsubstantiated.
Locked constraints and empty rules must be preserved exactly; any penalty-based encoding could alter semantics.
excerpts./rationale: The search candidate is kernel.py lines 10-13, function complete. It enumerates product((False, True), repeat=size) and returns the first list satisfying conforms, or None. excerpts./plan/formulation: QUBO/Ising equivalent of maximizing the signed pair score. Let x_i=1 if member i is in group True, else 0. For each preference pair (i,j,w) with w=+1 for apart and w=-1 for together, contribution = w*(2*(x_i xor x_j)-1) = w*(2x_i+2x_j-4x_i x_j-1). Hence score = constant + sum_i h_i x_i + sum_{i<j} Q_ij x_i x_j with h_i = 2*sum_{j!=i} w_ij, Q_ij = -4*w_ij, constant = -sum_{i<j} w_ij. Maximize this QUBO (or minimize its negation); all 2^n assignments are feasible because groups may be empty and there are no capacity constraints.
excerpts./plan/input_encoding: One binary variable/qubit per member, ordered as in validated `members`. Map x_i=0 to False and x_i=1 to True, or Ising x_i=(1-Z_i)/2 if using Z operators. Because sampling may miss the global optimum, exactness requires an additional exact fallback or verification, which is unresolved.

No constraint penalties are needed because the contract has no capacity or group-size constraints and empty groups are allowed.
